messages:
maria: Quick async standup for today — GPU fleet / provisioning / quota check (what I did / blockers / plan). TL;DR: regional buffer OK but AMS spot attrition higher than expected.

alex: What I did: validated prewarm jobs in us-east-1, bumped pool size +2. No immediate errors.

alex: Blockers: seeing 10-15% higher startup latency for p4d instances when cold; suspect driver mismatch on a small subset.

maria: Thanks. Can you drop the node list? I can kick a targeted drain.

alex: Pasted node IDs in infra playbook channel. Also opened a quick ticket: INFRA-3481.

priya: What I did: ran quota audit for EU regions. Found a quota shadow in eu-west-1 for g4dn that wasn’t accounted in our allocator. Raised case with cloud provider.

priya: Blockers: provider case says 24–48h response. If quota doesn’t come through we’ll need to re-route some prewarms to eu-central-1.

sam: What I did: adjusted autoscaler policy to allow short bursts (max surge +15%) during prewarm windows. Deployed change at 07:20 UTC.

sam: Blockers: unit tests for surge calculation flaky, will stabilize in PR #2567. Pinged @oliver for review.

oliver: On it, will review today. Also ran a quick capacity sim — if eu-west-1 stays down we can absorb ~120 concurrent requests before latency SLOs degrade.

maria: Plan: 1) Alex — drain and reprovision the 3 bad p4d nodes (target window 09:00 UTC). 2) Priya — monitor quota case; if not resolved by 16:00 UTC, start eu-central reroute. 3) Sam/Oliver — merge surge PR once tests green. 4) I’ll increase AMS spot buffer by +1 in the meantime.

maria: Risk: if provider case delays, we may hit quota limits for weekend load test. Recommend we throttle non-critical prewarms and prioritize customer reserved pools.

infra-bot: AUTO: prewarm-job-check: all jobs scheduled, 3 warnings in eu-west-1 (quota shadow). See https://internal.redwood.ai/runs/7864

alex: Quick note: I’m going to run `sudo nvidia-smi -pm 1` and reprovision drivers on the 3 nodes and monitor for 2 cycles. Will update here when done.

priya: Also tagging @maria — opened a follow-up to create a fallback routing rule in the router config: `route.region_fallback = [eu-central-1, us-east-1]` — needs approval for rollout.

maria: Approved for canary (5% traffic). Sam — create canary rollout with rollback hook.

sam: Will do. Putting canary in at 12:30 UTC.

oliver: FYI I ran an eval on batching impact — enabling aggressive batching on non-interactive jobs drops tokens/s cost by ~18% with minimal p99 impact. Might be a useful lever if quotas constrain us.

maria: Good point. Add that to the ops playbook as option C.

alex: Update: driver reprovision done, two nodes back to normal, one still shows intermittent CUDA init failures. Rebooting now.

maria: Thanks. Keep updates short here. If anyone wants to pair on the failing node ping me and I’ll jump in. :thumbsup:

oliver: Minor ask — can we add a simple dashboard widget for 'quota-shadow' alerts by region? Will help ops triage quickly.

priya: Agree. Filing dashboard ticket INFRA-DASH-92.

maria: Closing notes: follow the plan above, update this thread after major steps. If quota case resolves early, we’ll revert the extra AMS spot buffer.

alex: Reboot completed — node healthy. Marking INFRA-3481 as investigating->in-progress.

sam: Canary rollout scheduled. I’ll post results in ~30m.

infra-bot: DEPLOY: canary-rollout/route-fallback deployed to 5% (id: cr-9123) — monitoring for 15m.

maria: Nice. Thanks team.
